passages.text: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town.
passages.sermon: Jesus got into a boat.\r\nHe crossed over the water.\r\nHe came to His own town.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον διεπέρασεν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πόλιν

passages.text: Just then some men brought to Him a paralytic lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in His own town.
Some men brought a paralyzed man to Jesus.
The paralyzed man lay on a mat.
Jesus saw the faith of these men.
Jesus spoke to the paralyzed man.
Jesus said, “Take courage, son.”
Jesus said, “Your sins are forgiven.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παραλυτικὸν ἐπὶ κλίνης βεβλημένον καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν τῷ παραλυτικῷ Θάρσει τέκνον ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι

passages.text: On seeing this, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming!”
passages.sermon:
Some scribes watched Jesus.
They saw what He did.
They spoke quietly to themselves.
They said, “This man is blaspheming.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδού τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Οὗτος βλασφημεῖ

passages.text: But Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus can perceive people’s thoughts.
Some scribes thought to themselves that Jesus was blaspheming.
Jesus knew their thoughts.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?”
passages.original: Καὶ εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἵνα‿ τί ἐνθυμεῖσθε πονηρὰ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν

passages.text: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes.
Jesus asked them a question.
He said, "Which is easier to say?"
He gave two choices.
The first is, "Your sins are forgiven."
The second is, "Get up and walk?"
passages.original: τί γάρ ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον εἰπεῖν Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἢ εἰπεῖν Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει

passages.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” Then He said to the paralytic, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus has authority on earth.
Jesus can forgive sins.
Jesus wanted people to know this.
Jesus spoke to the paralyzed man.
Jesus said, “Get up.”
Jesus said, “Pick up your mat.”
Jesus said, “Go home.”
passages.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας τότε λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ Ἐγερθεὶς ἆρόν σου τὴν κλίνην καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου

passages.text: And the man got up and went home.
passages.sermon:
The man was paralyzed.
Jesus spoke to the man.
The man stood up.
The man picked up his mat.
The man went to his house.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
passages.sermon:
The crowds saw what happened.
They felt awe.
They glorified God.
God had given such authority to men.
passages.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐφοβήθησαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν Θεὸν τὸν δόντα ἐξουσίαν τοιαύτην τοῖς ἀνθρώποις

passages.text: As Jesus went on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Matthew got up and followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked away from that place.
He saw a man.
The man’s name was Matthew.
Matthew sat at the tax booth.
Jesus spoke to Matthew.
Jesus said, “Follow Me.”
Matthew stood up.
Matthew followed Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ παράγων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον Μαθθαῖον λεγόμενον καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἀκολούθει μοι καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Later, as Jesus was dining at Matthew’s house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Him and His disciples.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in Matthew’s house.
Jesus was eating a meal there.
Many tax collectors came to the house.
Many sinners also came.
These tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus.
They ate with Jesus and His disciples.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ ἰδοὺ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐλθόντες συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When the Pharisees saw this, they asked His disciples, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees saw Jesus eating with tax collectors and sinners.
The Pharisees spoke to Jesus’ disciples.
The Pharisees asked a question.
They said, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
passages.original: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν

passages.text: On hearing this, Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard what the Pharisees said.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Healthy people do not need a doctor.
Sick people need a doctor.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας εἶπεν Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλ’ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες

passages.text: But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He told them to go and learn something important.
He said, “I desire mercy, not sacrifice.”
Jesus explained His purpose.
He said, “I have not come to call the righteous.”
He said, “I have come to call sinners.”
passages.original: πορευθέντες δὲ μάθετε τί ἐστιν Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς

passages.text: At that time John’s disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast so often, but Your disciples do not fast?”
passages.sermon:
John’s disciples came to Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “We fast often.”
They said, “The Pharisees also fast often.”
They said, “But your disciples do not fast.”
passages.original: Τότε προσέρχονται αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου λέγοντες Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύομεν πολλά οἱ δὲ μαθηταί σου οὐ νηστεύουσιν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while He is with them? But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to John’s disciples.
He answered their question about fasting.
He said, “The guests of the bridegroom cannot mourn while the bridegroom is with them.
The bridegroom is present with them now.
But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them.
Then the guests will fast.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος πενθεῖν ἐφ’ ὅσον μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ὁ νυμφίος ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν

passages.text: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. For the patch will pull away from the garment, and a worse tear will result.
passages.sermon: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment.\r\nThe patch will pull away from the garment.\r\nA worse tear will result.
passages.original: Οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐπιβάλλει ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπὶ ἱματίῳ παλαιῷ αἴρει γὰρ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱματίου καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται

passages.text: Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will burst, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His listeners.
He explained a simple truth.
People do not pour new wine into old wineskins.
If they pour new wine into old wineskins, the wineskins will burst.
The wine will spill out.
The wineskins will be ruined.
Instead, people pour new wine into new wineskins.
Both the wine and the wineskins are preserved.
passages.original: Οὐδὲ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς εἰ δὲ μή¦γε ῥήγνυνται οἱ ἀσκοί καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἐκχεῖται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπόλλυνται ἀλλὰ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς καὶ ἀμφότεροι συντηροῦνται

passages.text: While Jesus was saying these things, a synagogue leader came and knelt before Him. “My daughter has just died,” he said. “But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was speaking to the people.
A synagogue leader came to Jesus.
The leader knelt before Jesus.
He said, “My daughter has just died.”
He said, “Come and place Your hand on her.”
He said, “She will live.”
passages.original: Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτοῖς ἰδοὺ ἄρχων εἷς ἐλθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ μου ἄρτι ἐτελεύτησεν ἀλλὰ ἐλθὼν ἐπίθες τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐπ’ αὐτήν καὶ ζήσεται

passages.text: So Jesus got up and went with him, along with His disciples.
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard the synagogue leader’s request.
Jesus stood up.
Jesus followed the synagogue leader.
Jesus’ disciples also followed Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Suddenly a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind Him and touched the fringe of His cloak.
passages.sermon: A woman had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.\r\nShe came up behind Jesus.\r\nShe touched the edge of His cloak.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ αἱμορροοῦσα δώδεκα ἔτη προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ

passages.text: She said to herself, “If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.”
passages.sermon:
A woman had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She came up behind Jesus.
She spoke to herself.
She said, “If I only touch His cloak, I will be healed.”
passages.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ἐν ἑαυτῇ Ἐὰν μόνον ἅψωμαι τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι

passages.text: Jesus turned and saw her. “Take courage, daughter,” He said, “your faith has healed you.” And the woman was cured from that very hour.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the woman.
Jesus turned to her.
Jesus spoke to her.
Jesus said, “Take courage, daughter.”
Jesus said, “Your faith has healed you.”
The woman was healed at that moment.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς στραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν εἶπεν Θάρσει θύγατερ ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε καὶ ἐσώθη ἡ γυνὴ ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης

passages.text: When Jesus entered the house of the synagogue leader, He saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.
passages.sermon: Jesus entered the house of the synagogue leader.\r\nHe saw the flute players.\r\nHe saw the noisy crowd.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἄρχοντος καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς αὐλητὰς καὶ τὸν ὄχλον θορυβούμενον

passages.text: “Go away,” He told them. “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” And they laughed at Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd.
He said, “Go away.”
He said, “The girl is not dead.”
He said, “She is asleep.”
The people laughed at Jesus.
passages.original: ἔλεγεν Ἀναχωρεῖτε οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν τὸ κοράσιον ἀλλὰ καθεύδει καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ

passages.text: After the crowd had been put outside, Jesus went in and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
\r\nThe crowd was inside the house.
\r\nSomeone put the crowd outside.
\r\nJesus entered the house.
\r\nJesus took the girl by the hand.
\r\nThe girl got up.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἐξεβλήθη ὁ ὄχλος εἰσελθὼν ἐκράτησεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς καὶ ἠγέρθη τὸ κοράσιον

passages.text: And the news about this spread throughout that region.
passages.sermon: People heard what Jesus did.\r\nThe news spread everywhere in that region.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ φήμη αὕτη εἰς ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἐκείνην

passages.text: As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed Him, crying out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus left that place.
Two blind men followed Jesus.
The two blind men cried out.
They said, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
passages.original: Καὶ παράγοντι ἐκεῖθεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ δύο τυφλοὶ κράζοντες καὶ λέγοντες Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς υἱὸς Δαυίδ

passages.text: After Jesus had entered the house, the blind men came to Him. “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” He asked. “Yes, Lord,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered the house.
Two blind men came to Jesus.
Jesus spoke to the blind men.
Jesus asked, “Do you believe I am able to do this?”
The blind men answered Jesus.
They said, “Yes, Lord.”
passages.original: Ἐλθόντι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ τυφλοί καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πιστεύετε ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ναί Κύριε

passages.text: Then He touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith will it be done to you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the two blind men.
He touched their eyes.
He spoke to them.
He said, “According to your faith, it will be done for you.”
passages.original: Τότε ἥψατο τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν λέγων Κατὰ τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν γενηθήτω ὑμῖν

passages.text: And their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them sternly, “See that no one finds out about this!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed the blind men.
He opened their eyes.
They could see.
Jesus spoke to them very firmly.
He warned them.
He said, “Do not let anyone know about this.”
passages.original: καὶ ἠνεῴχθησαν αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί καὶ ἐνεβριμήθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Ὁρᾶτε μηδεὶς γινωσκέτω

passages.text: But they went out and spread the news about Him throughout the land.
passages.sermon:
Two men had just received healing from Jesus.
They left the place where Jesus was.
They began to tell others about Jesus.
They spread the news about Jesus everywhere in that region.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες διεφήμισαν αὐτὸν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ

passages.text: As they were leaving, a demon-possessed man who was mute was brought to Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present.
Some people were leaving.
Other people brought a man to Jesus.
This man could not speak.
An evil spirit possessed this man.
passages.original: Αὐτῶν δὲ ἐξερχομένων ἰδοὺ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπον κωφὸν δαιμονιζόμενον

passages.text: And when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus met a man who could not speak.
A demon possessed this man.
Jesus drove out the demon.
The man began to speak.
The crowds saw this happen.
The crowds felt amazed.
The crowds said, “Nothing like this has ever happened in Israel.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐκβληθέντος τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες Οὐδέποτε ἐφάνη οὕτως ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: But the Pharisees said, “It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons.”
passages.sermon: The Pharisees were religious leaders in Israel.\r\nThe Pharisees spoke about Jesus.\r\nThey said, “He drives out demons by the prince of demons.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον Ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια

passages.text: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled through every town and village.
He taught in their synagogues.
He preached the good news about the kingdom.
He healed every disease.
He healed every sickness.
passages.original: Καὶ περιῆγεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς πόλεις πάσας καὶ τὰς κώμας διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν

passages.text: When He saw the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the crowds.
Jesus felt deep compassion for the crowds.
The crowds were harassed.
The crowds were helpless.
The crowds were like sheep without a shepherd.
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἐσπλαγχνίσθη περὶ αὐτῶν ὅτι ἦσαν ἐσκυλμένοι καὶ ἐρριμμένοι ὡσεὶ πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα

passages.text: Then He said to His disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “The harvest is plentiful.\r\nBut the workers are few.”
passages.original: Τότε λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι

passages.text: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them to pray.
He said, “Ask the Lord of the harvest.
Ask Him to send out workers.
Ask Him to send workers into His harvest.”
passages.original: δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ Κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐκβάλῃ ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ
